title: Local Redirect Policy `addressMatcher` no longer overrides an existing Service (from 1.17.16)

detection.reason: read from the agent's Cilium projection (feature names, never the policy's values); needs Cilium collection switched on in Integrations

quote: `CiliumLocalRedirectPolicy` with `addressMatcher` will no longer override an existing Service at the same frontend address.
remediation: For each policy the command lists whose frontend address is also a Service's ClusterIP, migrate to `serviceMatcher`. `--enable-lrp-address-matcher-override=true` restores the old behaviour on 1.17.16+ only: the flag does not exist in 1.18 or later, and 1.18.10+ / 1.19.4+ enforce the same guard with no override (upstream ships no 1.18/1.19 upgrade note for it), so migrate instead of relying on the flag.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumlocalredirectpolicies.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.redirectFrontend.addressMatcher != null) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row uses addressMatcher

title: Agent liveness probe no longer checks Kubernetes apiserver connectivity (from 1.17.4)

detection.reason: probe behaviour

quote: The check for connectivity to the Kubernetes apiserver has been removed from the cilium-agent liveness probe.
remediation: An agent that loses the apiserver is no longer restarted by its liveness probe. Set Helm `livenessProbe.requireK8sConnectivity=true` to keep the old behaviour (1.16.10+ has the same setting but defaults it to true, so every 1.16 cluster changes on this upgrade).

title: Operator Kubernetes client rate limit is now configured separately from the agent's

detection.reason: the option's VALUE is not collected (cilium-config ships key names only)

quote: The Kubernetes clients used by Cilium Agent and Cilium Operator now have separately configurable rate limits.
remediation: Only matters if you raised `k8s-client-qps` / `k8s-client-burst` (Helm `k8sClientRateLimit.qps/burst`) above 100 / 200: from 1.17 those apply to the agent only and the operator uses 100 QPS / 200 burst unless you also set `operator-k8s-client-qps` / `operator-k8s-client-burst` (Helm `k8sClientRateLimit.operator.*`). Lower or unset values need nothing — the operator's default went up.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(k8s-client-qps|k8s-client-burst|operator-k8s-client-qps|operator-k8s-client-burst)$")) | "\(.key)=\(.value)"'  # k8s-client-qps above 100 or burst above 200 without the operator-* keys is affected

title: Consul kvstore support removed

detection.reason: the option's VALUE is not collected (cilium-config ships key names only)

quote: Support for Consul, deprecated since v1.12, has been removed.
remediation: If cilium-config `kvstore` is `consul`, move to etcd or CRD-backed identities before upgrading; the 1.17 agent cannot start.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(kvstore)$")) | "\(.key)=\(.value)"'  # kvstore=consul is affected

title: Service protocol differentiation on by default; downgrades need care

detection.reason: datapath / runtime behaviour — nothing in the collected inventory states it

quote: Cilium now supports services protocol differentiation
remediation: Existing services keep working; delete and re-create a Service to have its protocol considered. Before downgrading below 1.17, read the note: protocol-differentiated services must be handled first. `bpf-lb-proto-diff: "false"` turns the feature off.

title: MTU auto-detection now uses the lowest MTU of all external interfaces

detection.reason: cilium-config keys only (names, never values): an option passed on the agent or operator command line (extraArgs) or in a ConfigMap of another name is not scanned; only the presence of an explicit mtu is read

quote: MTU auto-detection will now use the lowest MTU of all external interfaces.
remediation: cilium-config does not pin `mtu`, so on nodes with several external interfaces the pod MTU can drop to the smallest one (e.g. a 1500 management NIC next to a 9001 data NIC). Set Helm `MTU` explicitly if that is not what you want.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.name'  # then on a node: ip -o link | grep -v lxc  (compare the external interfaces' MTUs)

title: L7 visibility Pod annotation `policy.cilium.io/proxy-visibility` removed
quote: Support for L7 protocol visibility using Pod annotations (`policy.cilium.io/proxy-visibility`), deprecated since v1.15, has been removed.
remediation: Replace the annotation on the Pods named with an L7 network policy on the same ports; the annotation does nothing from 1.17.

title: Cluster name validation can no longer be bypassed

detection.reason: the option's VALUE is not collected (cilium-config ships key names only)

quote: The Cilium cluster name validation cannot be bypassed anymore, both for the local and remote clusters.
remediation: If the command prints a row, rename the cluster to at most 32 lower-case alphanumerics and '-' (starting and ending alphanumeric) before upgrading; in a Cluster Mesh, remote cluster names are validated too. `upgradeCompatibility` no longer defers it.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .metadata.namespace as $ns | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key == "cluster-name") | select(.value | test("^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,30}[a-z0-9])?$") | not) | "\($ns)/cilium-config cluster-name=\(.value)"'  # a row is a cluster name the agent will refuse

title: Managed etcd support removed

detection.reason: whether the kvstore is the chart-managed etcd is decided by Helm values

quote: This support, which had been previously deprecated as complicated and error prone, has now been removed.
remediation: If the cluster still runs the cilium-etcd-operator (the workloads named), move to CRD-backed identities or an externally managed etcd before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?; .image | test("cilium-etcd-operator"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # a row is a managed etcd that must be replaced

title: IPsec: single-key mode removed — per-tunnel keys always

detection.reason: cilium-config keys only (names, never values): an option passed on the agent or operator command line (extraArgs) or in a ConfigMap of another name is not scanned; the key is written when IPsec encryption is enabled

quote: For IPsec, support for a single key has been removed.
remediation: IPsec is enabled. If the command prints `per-tunnel=false`, rotate the key to the per-tunnel format before upgrading (the 1.16 note already required it); the command prints only the format, never the key.
verifyCommand: kubectl get daemonset,secret -A -o json | jq -r '.items as $i | [$i[] | select(.kind == "DaemonSet") | .metadata.namespace as $ns | .spec.template.spec.volumes[]? | select(.name == "cilium-ipsec-secrets") | {ns: $ns, n: .secret.secretName}] | unique[] | . as $v | ([$i[] | select(.kind == "Secret" and .metadata.namespace == $v.ns and .metadata.name == $v.n)] | first) as $s | if $s == null then "\($v.ns)/\($v.n) MISSING" else "\($v.ns)/\($v.n) per-tunnel=\([$s.data[]? | @base64d | test("^[0-9]+\\+")] | (length != 0) and all)" end'  # per-tunnel=false must be rotated first; MISSING means the agent mounts a Secret that does not exist; no row means no IPsec key volume

title: MetalLB-based BGP (`bgp.enabled`, `bgp-announce-*`) removed — use the BGP control plane

detection.reason: cilium-config keys only (names, never values): an option passed on the agent or operator command line (extraArgs) or in a ConfigMap of another name is not scanned

quote: Support for `metallb-bgp`, deprecated since 1.14, has been removed.
remediation: cilium-config still configures the MetalLB BGP integration. Recreate the peering with the Cilium BGP control plane (`bgpControlPlane.enabled` + CiliumBGPClusterConfig / CiliumBGPPeerConfig) BEFORE upgrading; on 1.17 nothing announces LoadBalancer IPs or pod CIDRs and they become unreachable from outside.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .metadata.namespace as $ns | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(bgp-config-path|bgp-announce-lb-ip|bgp-announce-pod-cidr)$")) | "\($ns)/cilium-config \(.key)=\(.value)"'  # each row is an option still set in cilium-config
coversNotes: Removed Options: The previously deprecated `metallb-bgp` flags `bgp-config-path`
Helm Options: The `metallb-bgp` integration Helm options `bgp.enabled`

title: Cassandra and Memcached L7 policies deprecated

detection.reason: read from the agent's Cilium projection (feature names, never the policy's values); needs Cilium collection switched on in Integrations

quote: Layer 7 policy support for Cassandra and Memcached have been deprecated
remediation: Plan to replace the L7 rules in the policies listed with L3/L4 rules.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io,ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $p | [(.spec // empty), (.specs[]?)] | map(((.ingress // []) + (.egress // []) + (.ingressDeny // []) + (.egressDeny // []))[]) | select(any(.[]; (.toPorts // []) | any((.rules.l7proto? // "") | test("^(cassandra|memcache)")))) | $p | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row uses a Cassandra or Memcached L7 parser

title: TLS visibility Secrets now read only from the configured secrets namespace

detection.reason: read from the agent's Cilium projection (feature names, never the policy's values); needs Cilium collection switched on in Integrations

quote: TLS Visibility can now pass secrets to Envoy via SDS instead of inline via NPDS.
remediation: `tls.readSecretsOnlyFromSecretsNamespace` defaults to true. With `tls.secretSync.enabled: true` (the default for NEW clusters) the operator copies the Secrets referenced by `terminatingTLS` / `originatingTLS` into `tls.secretsNamespace` for you. With `upgradeCompatibility: 1.16` (or `tls.secretSync.enabled=false`) nothing copies them: for the policies listed, copy the Secrets into `tls.secretsNamespace` before upgrading, or set `tls.readSecretsOnlyFromSecretsNamespace=false`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io,ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $p | [(.spec // empty), (.specs[]?)] | map(((.ingress // []) + (.egress // []) + (.ingressDeny // []) + (.egressDeny // []))[]) | select(any(.[]; (.toPorts // []) | any(.terminatingTLS != null or .originatingTLS != null))) | $p | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row references TLS Secrets
